A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MASNET research. Complete text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The reduction from 33 to 32 pages comes from reference reflow, without loss of scientific content.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original set-containment and monotone-function approximation experiments. Appendix D contains additional evaluations and ablations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the original experimental results, including synthetic, text and point-cloud evaluations and ablation studies.

M1.justification: The MASNET architecture, Hat/ReLU/TRI/INT variants, parameterizations and training objectives are unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic data, MSWEB, MSNBC, Amazon Bedding/Feeding and ModelNet40 coverage, alongside the same monotone-function approximation task. Appendix evaluation scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: DeepSets and SetTransformer remain in the synthetic and approximation comparisons, with FlexSubNet and Neural SFE also retained in the text and main point-cloud comparisons. Appendix comparator sets also match.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same splits, class ratios, noise levels, embedding dimensions, point-cloud encoders and evaluation metrics. No experimental setting or protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The cardinality sweeps in Figures 4, 8 and 9, shallow/deep activation comparisons in Table 11, and outer-map and division-scaling ablations in Table 12 are identical.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including Table 7's ± entries. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-test information is added or removed.

E6.justification: All corresponding numerical entries and plotted results match. For example, Table 7 retains MASNET-Hat MAE of 0.00959 ± 0.00016, and Appendix D's Tables 10–14 contain identical scores.

T1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendices B–C retain identical definitions, dimension bounds, nonexistence results, Hölder and probability guarantees, universality arguments and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about MAS characterization, weakly MAS neural models, stability, monotone universality and empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Section 7's limitations are identical, including the restriction of probabilistic guarantees to randomized parameters, finite-ground-set universality and the unaddressed subgraph extension.

D1.justification: The implementation link, Appendix C's architecture and parameterization details, and Appendix D's hardware and dataset-preparation disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 40 works remain cited, and the related-work discussions in Section 1 and Appendix A are identical. Changes to publication years, venues, author names and title wording are bibliographic revisions, not changes in cited-work identity or research positioning.

P1.justification: Edits are confined to reference wording and the arXiv version/date stamp. Conference venues are abbreviated, some bibliographic details are omitted and several metadata fields are revised; scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened references reflow from three pages to two, moving the appendix start from page 14 to page 13. Matched scientific pages retain identical figures, tables, captions, axes, legends and layout apart from page numbers.

improvement.justification: The shorter, more uniform bibliography omits some bibliographic detail, while retaining the same cited works. Methods, proofs, experimental evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility disclosures are unchanged, so these limited editorial changes produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
